fact.claim: If you get eligible dividends from a Canadian company in a regular taxable account, you report 138% of what you were actually paid as income. You then get a dividend tax credit that lowers your tax, so at the same pre-tax amount you usually keep more from dividends than from GIC interest, which is taxed in full as ordinary income. None of this applies inside a TFSA or RRSP, where neither is taxed this way. The bigger grossed-up income can also reduce income-tested benefits, and a dividend is not guaranteed the way a GIC rate is.
